1) kubectl describe \u003ckind\u003e \u0: 1) Run kubectl describe <kind> <name> -n <ns> and compare generation with observedGeneration; 2) Check whether kube-controller-manager is healthy — a stalled controller is the most common cause; 3) Look for errors about this object in the controller-manager log; 4) Confirm apiserver and etcd are healthy; once the controller recovers, generation catches up automatically.
1) kubectl describe deploy \u003cname\u0: 1) Run kubectl describe deploy <name> -n <ns> for Conditions and Events; 2) Run kubectl get pod -n <ns> -l <selector> to see the state and reason of the unready Pods; 3) Common causes are insufficient resources for scheduling, image pull failures, and failing readiness probes; 4) Follow the Pod's specific state; for resource shortage, add nodes or lower requests.
1) kubectl describe ds \u003cname\u003e: 1) Run kubectl describe ds <name> -n <ns> for Events and desired/current counts; 2) Compare node taints against the DaemonSet's tolerations — a taint mismatch is the most common cause; 3) Check whether nodeSelector/affinity excludes those nodes; 4) For resource shortage, lower the DaemonSet's requests or free node resources.
1) kubectl describe hpa \u003cname\u003e: 1) Run kubectl describe hpa <name> -n <ns> and read the reason in Conditions; 2) ScalingLimited means it hit the min/max boundary; FailedGetScale means the target workload has a problem; 3) For metric failures, check whether metrics-server or the custom metrics adapter is healthy; 4) If new replicas stay Pending for lack of resources, add nodes.

1) Run kubectl describe hpa <name> -n <ns> to see the gap between the current and target metric; 2) Confirm the cluster still has resources for more replicas (node headroom); 3) With headroom, raise maxReplicas; without it, add nodes first; 4) Also assess whether per-replica capacity is too low — optimising the application beats scaling replicas indefinitely.
1) kubectl describe node \u003cnode\u003: 1) Run kubectl describe node <node> for Conditions and Events to tell MemoryPressure, DiskPressure and a lost kubelet apart; 2) Log in to the node and check kubelet and the container runtime (systemctl status kubelet containerd); 3) Use journalctl -u kubelet -n 200 to locate the problem; 4) If the node cannot recover soon, run kubectl drain so the Pods move promptly instead of waiting for the eviction timeout.

1) Run kubectl describe node <node> and read the timeline of Condition changes; 2) On the node, check the kubelet log — common root causes are resource pressure, a stalled container runtime, or an unstable network to apiserver; 3) While it flaps, kubectl cordon the node so no new Pods land on it; 4) Uncordon only after the root cause is fixed — do not repeatedly restart kubelet during the flapping.
1) kubectl describe node | grep -A5 'All: 1) Run kubectl describe node | grep -A5 'Allocated resources' to sum up allocation per node; 2) This is a capacity planning signal rather than an immediate outage — assess whether there is still headroom to absorb a node failure; 3) Check for Pods with requests set far above actual usage; lowering them frees a lot of schedulable capacity; 4) If headroom is genuinely insufficient, add nodes.
1) kubectl describe pod \u003cpod\u003e: 1) Run kubectl describe pod <pod> -n <ns> and use the Event timestamps to see whether it is stuck pulling the image, mounting a volume, or in an init container; 2) For slow pulls, check image size and registry bandwidth, and consider pre-warming images or a local registry; 3) For slow mounts, check the PV/CSI driver state; 4) If the application itself starts slowly, optimise startup and set a sensible readiness probe initialDelaySeconds.

1) Run kubectl describe pod <pod> -n <ns> and read the Waiting Reason; 2) For ImagePullBackOff, check the image name, tag and pull credentials (imagePullSecrets); 3) For CreateContainerConfigError, check the referenced ConfigMap/Secret exists; 4) For CrashLoopBackOff, follow the crash loop path and read the --previous logs.
1) kubectl describe pv \u003cpv\u003e 与: 1) Run kubectl describe pv <pv> and kubectl describe pvc <pvc> -n <ns> and read the errors in Events; 2) Common causes are an unavailable storage backend, insufficient capacity, or wrong StorageClass parameters; 3) Check whether the CSI driver Pods are healthy (usually in kube-system); 4) For a storage backend failure, follow that system's own procedure — Pods stay Pending meanwhile.
1) kubectl describe quota -n \u003cns\u0: 1) Run kubectl describe quota -n <ns> to see which item (cpu/memory/pods/storage) topped out; 2) Use kubectl get pod -n <ns> -o custom-columns to sum requests per workload and find the biggest consumers; 3) Check for stopped-but-uncleaned resources still holding quota; 4) If more quota is genuinely needed, ask the cluster admin to adjust the ResourceQuota.
1) kubectl exec 进入使用该卷的 Pod，用 df -i 确认；2: 1) kubectl exec into a Pod using the volume and run df -i; 2) Count files level by level to find the directories with the most small files; 3) Clean up useless small files (cache fragments, temporary files); 4) If it cannot be reduced, expand the volume or change storage type.
1) kubectl get apiservice 看哪个 APIService: 1) Run kubectl get apiservice to see which APIService is False; 2) Run kubectl describe apiservice <name> for the specific error; 3) If the backing service is down, check its Deployment/Service health (commonly metrics-server); 4) For certificate problems, verify the CA bundle configuration.
1) kubectl get apiservice 看哪个处于 False 状态: 1) Run kubectl get apiservice to see which one is False; 2) Run kubectl describe apiservice <name> for the specific error; 3) If the backing service is down, check its Deployment/Service; 4) For certificate problems, verify the CA bundle configuration.
1) kubectl get apiservice 确认是哪个 APIServi: 1) Run kubectl get apiservice to identify the APIService; 2) Run kubectl -n <ns> get pod to check its backing Pods; 3) Read that Pod's logs for startup or runtime errors; 4) After recovery, verify with something like kubectl top node that the functionality is back.
1) kubectl get job \u003cjob\u003e -n \u: 1) Run kubectl get job <job> -n <ns> for the failure count, then kubectl logs job/<job> for the reason; 2) Run kubectl describe job for Events and whether it gave up after exhausting backoffLimit; 3) After fixing the root cause, kubectl delete job and resubmit, or let the CronJob run again on schedule; 4) Confirm whether the failure has downstream impact (missing output, skipped cleanup) and redo it manually if needed.

1) Run kubectl get job <job> -n <ns> for elapsed time and completions; 2) Run kubectl logs job/<job> to see where it is stuck; 3) Determine whether the task is genuinely long-running or hung — for a hang, kubectl delete job, fix it and rerun; 4) Set a sensible activeDeadlineSeconds so Jobs cannot hang indefinitely.
1) kubectl get node -o wide 看各节点 kubelet: 1) Run kubectl get node -o wide for kubelet versions and kubectl version for the control plane; 2) Confirm the skew is within the officially supported window (kubelet must not exceed apiserver and must not lag by more than two minor versions); 3) This usually means an unfinished upgrade — bring the lagging nodes up to date; 4) Before upgrading, confirm workload compatibility with the new API versions.
1) kubectl get pod -A -o wide --field-se: 1) Run kubectl get pod -A -o wide --field-selector spec.nodeName=<node> | wc -l for the actual count; 2) Compare against the kubelet maxPods setting (110 by default); 3) Use kubectl drain or scheduling policy to move some Pods to other nodes; 4) If you genuinely need higher density, raise maxPods but reassess node CPU/memory/PLEG pressure at the same time.
1) kubectl get pod -n \u003cns\u003e -l: 1) Run kubectl get pod -n <ns> -l <selector> -o wide to see which nodes they landed on; 2) Check whether the DaemonSet's nodeSelector/affinity matches the node labels; 3) This usually follows a node label change or a DaemonSet update — after correcting it the extra Pods are cleaned up automatically; 4) Delete any leftovers manually.

1) Run kubectl get pod -n <ns> -l <selector> and check by ordinal which replica is stuck; 2) Run kubectl describe pod to check whether its PVC bound successfully — this is the most common sticking point for stateful services; 3) For storage problems, check the PV/StorageClass and the CSI driver; 4) For application problems check kubectl logs; once fixed, the StatefulSet continues automatically.
1) kubectl get pod \u003cpod\u003e -n \u: 1) Run kubectl get pod <pod> -n <ns> -o wide for STATUS and READY, then kubectl describe pod for Events; 2) Pending usually means insufficient resources or scheduling constraints (affinity, taints, unbound PVC); for ImagePullBackOff check the image address and pull credentials; 3) Running but not Ready — check the readiness probe and kubectl logs <pod> for startup errors; 4) Confirm whether the replica count is now too low to carry traffic, and scale healthy replicas first if so.
1) kubectl get pvc -n \u003cns\u003e 定位对: 1) Run kubectl get pvc -n <ns> to find the PVC and PV; 2) kubectl exec into a Pod using the volume and use du to find the largest directories; 3) Clean up logs and temporary data; 4) If the StorageClass supports online expansion, kubectl edit pvc and raise spec.resources.requests.storage; otherwise migrate the data.
1) kubectl logs -n \u003cns\u003e deploy: 1) Run kubectl logs -n <ns> deploy/prometheus-operator for the specific error; 2) For permission errors, verify the Operator's ClusterRole covers the required resources; 3) For Reconcile/Sync failures, check the corresponding CRD objects (kubectl describe servicemonitor/prometheusrule); 4) For rejected resources, kubectl describe shows the rejection reason, usually failed field validation.
1) kubectl logs \u003cpod\u003e -c confi: 1) Run kubectl logs <pod> -c config-reloader -n <ns> for the specific error; 2) It is usually a config syntax error causing the reload to be rejected; 3) Validate with promtool check config / amtool check-config; 4) After fixing, confirm the reload succeeded and verify the new config on Prometheus's /config page.
1) kubectl logs \u003cpod\u003e -n \u003: 1) Run kubectl logs <pod> -n <ns> --previous to see the log before the last exit — this is the key step; 2) Run kubectl describe pod for the exit code and Events: 137 usually means OOM or killed, 1/2 usually means the application failed to start; 3) For config or dependency problems (unreachable database, missing ConfigMap/Secret), fix the dependency first; 4) For OOM, compare resources.limits.memory against actual usage, or fix the application's memory leak.
1) kubectl logs 或实例日志里找配置解析报错的具体行；2) 用 p: 1) Find the config parse error line in kubectl logs or the instance log; 2) Validate locally with promtool check config prometheus.yml; 3) On Kubernetes the config is usually generated by the Operator — check ServiceMonitor/PrometheusRule for invalid fields; 4) After fixing, confirm /-/reload succeeded and the /config page shows the new configuration.
1) kubectl rollout status deploy/\u003cn: 1) Run kubectl rollout status deploy/<name> -n <ns> to see which replica it is stuck on; 2) Run kubectl describe pod to see why the new Pod is not ready (image, probe, resources); 3) If it cannot be fixed quickly, kubectl rollout undo deploy/<name> to roll back; 4) After fixing, redeploy and review whether maxSurge/maxUnavailable are sensible.
1) kubectl rollout status ds/\u003cname\: 1) Run kubectl rollout status ds/<name> -n <ns> to see which nodes are stuck; 2) Run kubectl describe pod to see why the new Pod is not ready; 3) If it cannot be fixed quickly, kubectl rollout undo ds/<name>; 4) Check whether the updateStrategy maxUnavailable is too conservative.
1) kubectl rollout status sts/\u003cname: 1) Run kubectl rollout status sts/<name> -n <ns> to see which replica it is stuck on; 2) StatefulSets update in order, so one stuck replica blocks all the rest — focus on the one currently updating; 3) Run kubectl describe pod to find why it is not ready (PVC, probe, image); 4) If it cannot be fixed quickly, kubectl rollout undo.
1) kubectl top node 与 kubectl top pod -A: 1) Run kubectl top node and kubectl top pod -A --sort-by=memory to find the biggest consumers; 2) Check for Pods without a memory limit growing without bound; 3) Use kubectl drain to move some Pods off, confirming the target nodes have headroom; 4) Review the kubelet eviction thresholds, and add nodes if the cluster is tight overall.
1) kubectl top node 确认整体分布，kubectl top p: 1) Run kubectl top node for the overall picture and kubectl top pod -A --sort-by=cpu for the biggest consumers; 2) Check whether too many high-load Pods landed on this node and drain some if needed; 3) Check whether Pod requests are set too low, causing overcommit; 4) If the cluster is running hot overall, add nodes.
1) kubectl top pod \u003cpod\u003e -n \u: 1) Run kubectl top pod <pod> -n <ns> --containers and compare against resources.limits.cpu; 2) Note that runtimes like Java that do not detect the cgroup limit may spawn too many threads and worsen throttling — check the JVM version and flags; 3) Raise limits.cpu, or scale out horizontally with an HPA; 4) A limit far above the request is easily squeezed by overcommit — consider bringing them closer together.

1) Run kubectl top pod <pod> -n <ns> --containers to compare actual usage against the limit; 2) Check the CPUThrottlingHigh metric to confirm whether it is already being throttled; 3) For genuine growth, raise resources.limits.cpu or scale out with an HPA; 4) For abnormal usage, capture a CPU profile in the application rather than papering over it with more quota.

1) Run kubectl top pod <pod> -n <ns> --containers to compare usage against the limit; 2) Check the history curve to tell a steady climb (likely a leak) from a normal traffic peak; 3) For normal peaks, raise resources.limits.memory with headroom; 4) For a steady climb, capture a heap profile in the application — raising the quota only postpones it.
1) systemctl --failed 列出失败单元；2) journalc: 1) Run systemctl --failed to list the failed units; 2) Use journalctl -u <unit> -n 100 --no-pager to find the cause; 3) On Kubernetes nodes pay special attention to kubelet, containerd and kube-proxy; 4) After fixing, run systemctl reset-failed and confirm recovery.
1) 从告警标签定位是哪个组件/实例在报错；2) 看该组件日志中的具体错误码：4: 1) Use the alert labels to identify the component/instance that is erroring; 2) Read the specific error code in that component's log: 401/403 is an RBAC problem, 429 is throttling, 5xx is an apiserver-side problem; 3) For permissions, verify the ServiceAccount's Role/ClusterRoleBinding; 4) For throttling, check whether the component is doing high-frequency LIST calls and switch to Watch or add a resourceVersion.
1) 先 ping / ssh 确认机器本身是否存活，机器宕机按宕机处理；2): 1) First confirm the machine is alive with ping/ssh — if it is down, handle it as a host outage; 2) If it is alive, investigate the node's network and certificates to apiserver (the kubelet log states the error clearly); 3) Check whether any single-replica critical service runs on that node and start it elsewhere first; 4) After recovery, confirm the node is Ready again and Pod states are normal.
1) 在 /status 页看查询引擎的并发与队列指标；2) 用 topk 类查: 1) Check the query engine concurrency and queue metrics on the /status page; 2) Use topk-style queries or the query log to find the heaviest queries; 3) The usual root causes are high-cardinality labels and over-wide time ranges — narrow the range and reduce group by dimensions; 4) If it stays high after tuning, scale Prometheus or use federation/sharding.
1) 在 /targets 页找出被拒绝的目标与具体原因；2) 到目标侧确认为何: 1) Find the rejected targets and the specific reason on the /targets page; 2) On the target side, work out why the label count is so high — usually high-cardinality data (user ID, request ID) was made into labels; 3) Fix the metric design at the source, or drop the excess labels with metric_relabel_configs; 4) If more labels are genuinely needed, raise label_limit after assessing the cardinality impact.
1) 在 /targets 页找出被拒绝的目标与样本数；2) 手工 curl /: 1) Find the rejected targets and their sample counts on the /targets page; 2) Run curl /metrics | wc -l by hand to confirm the actual scale; 3) High-cardinality metrics are the main cause — reduce label dimensions at the source or drop unneeded metrics with metric_relabel_configs; 4) If a higher limit is genuinely needed, raise sample_limit after assessing storage and query impact.
1) 在 /targets 页找出被拒绝的目标；2) 手工 curl 该目标的: 1) Find the rejected targets on the /targets page; 2) curl that target's /metrics by hand to see the actual size and whether the metric count has ballooned; 3) High-cardinality metrics are the usual cause — fix at the source or drop with metric_relabel_configs; 4) If a higher limit is genuinely needed, raise body_size_limit.
1) 在 /targets 页找出被重复抓取的目标（同一实例出现在多个 job: 1) Find the duplicated targets on the /targets page (the same instance appearing under several jobs); 2) Check whether ServiceMonitor/PodMonitor selectors are too broad and overlapping; 3) Tighten the selectors so each target is scraped by exactly one job; 4) After fixing, confirm the discard counter stops growing.
1) 在 /targets 页确认当前目标数与限制；2) 检查 ServiceM: 1) Confirm the current target count against the limit on the /targets page; 2) Check whether the ServiceMonitor selector is too broad and picking up unwanted targets; 3) Tighten the selector or split across multiple Prometheus instances by business domain; 4) If more targets are genuinely needed, raise target_limit and size the resources accordingly.
1) 在 /targets 页确认是否所有目标都 down；2) 检查服务发现是: 1) Check on the /targets page whether every target is down; 2) Check that service discovery is working (the /service-discovery page); 3) If a config error left the target list empty, treat it as a configuration problem; 4) This is total monitoring blindness and should be the highest priority.
1) 在控制面节点确认 kube-apiserver 进程/静态 Pod 状态与: 1) On the control plane node, check the kube-apiserver process/static Pod state and logs; 2) For multi-replica deployments, confirm whether only some instances are down and whether the load balancer removed the faulty ones; 3) Common root causes are unavailable etcd, expired certificates and resource exhaustion; 4) Restore etcd and certificates first — apiserver usually recovers on its own.
1) 在控制面节点确认 kube-controller-manager 静态 P: 1) On the control plane node, check the kube-controller-manager static Pod or process state and logs; 2) For multi-replica deployments, confirm leader election is failing over correctly; 3) Common root causes are an unavailable apiserver or expired certificates; 4) After recovery, confirm workloads with wrong replica counts start self-healing.
1) 在控制面节点确认 kube-scheduler 静态 Pod 或进程状态与: 1) On the control plane node, check the kube-scheduler static Pod or process state and logs; 2) For multi-replica deployments, confirm whether it merely lost leadership and another replica can take over; 3) Common root causes are an unavailable apiserver or certificate problems; 4) After recovery, confirm Pending Pods start being scheduled.
1) 查看 apiserver 的 apiserver_flowcontrol: 1) Check the apiserver_flowcontrol metrics to see which flow schema is being throttled; 2) Identify the client making the flood of requests (usually an Operator or script doing full LIST calls); 3) Rate limit that client or fix its request pattern; 4) If more capacity is genuinely needed, tune the FlowSchema and PriorityLevelConfiguration.
1) 检查 Alertmanager 实例是否健康、网络是否连通；2) 在 Pr: 1) Check whether the Alertmanager instances are healthy and reachable; 2) Confirm Alertmanager discovery on the Prometheus /status page; 3) If the queue is full, check whether Alertmanager processing is stuck or the alert volume spiked abnormally; 4) After recovery, confirm Alertmanager actually received the alerts so nothing fails silently.
1) 检查 textfile 目录下的 .prom 文件权限与格式；2) 写入方: 1) Check the permissions and format of the .prom files in the textfile directory; 2) The writer is usually a cron script — confirm it succeeds and writes atomically (write .tmp then mv); 3) Validate format errors with promtool check metrics; 4) Clean up leftover temporary files, which break parsing.
1) 用 chronyc tracking 确认偏移量与上游源状态；2) 确认: 1) Run chronyc tracking to check the offset and upstream source state; 2) Confirm chronyd/ntpd is running and enabled at boot; 3) Check that 123/UDP to the NTP server is allowed; 4) For a large offset use chronyc makestep, then confirm all nodes agree on the time.
1) 用 df -h 定位挂载点，用 du -x --max-depth=1 逐: 1) Run df -h to find the mount point and du -x --max-depth=1 to drill into the largest directories; 2) For the container runtime directory (/var/lib/containerd or /var/lib/docker) run crictl rmi --prune to clean unused images; 3) Clean container logs (/var/log/pods) and confirm log rotation is working; 4) Use lsof +L1 for deleted files whose handles are still open.
1) 用 df -i 确认挂载点；2) 逐层统计文件数找出小文件最多的目录；3): 1) Run df -i to find the mount point; 2) Count files level by level to find the directories with the most small files; 3) On Kubernetes nodes it is usually container layers and log fragments — pruning unused images typically frees a lot of inodes; 4) Longer term, raise inode density or isolate small-file workloads to a dedicated partition.
1) 用 dmesg -T | grep -i 'killed process': 1) Run dmesg -T | grep -i 'killed process' to see which process was killed and how much memory it held; 2) Match it against kubectl get pod -A to find the Pod and whether its limit is set too low; 3) If the node is tight overall, move Pods off or add capacity; 4) Repeated kills require finding the application memory leak — raising the limit alone will just recur.
1) 用 dmesg -T | grep -i 'link is' 看抖动时间线: 1) Run dmesg -T | grep -i 'link is' for the flap timeline; 2) Check the cable and optical module — flapping usually means a bad physical connection; 3) Confirm the negotiated speed and duplex match the peer; 4) Ask the network team about the switch port state, or open a ticket in the cloud.
1) 用 du -x --max-depth=1 找出增长最快的目录；2) 确认: 1) Run du -x --max-depth=1 to find the fastest-growing directory; 2) Determine whether the growth is normal business or abnormal (an application looping on logs, backups piling up); 3) Prune unused images and container logs; 4) If the growth is genuine, plan disk expansion or data migration — do not wait until it is full.
1) 用 free -h 与 swapon -s 确认 swap 使用情况；2): 1) Run free -h and swapon -s to check swap usage; 2) Use smem or VmSwap in /proc/<pid>/status to find the processes swapped out most; 3) Kubernetes nodes should generally have swap disabled — leaving it on masks real memory pressure and breaks QoS; 4) The root cause is insufficient memory, so follow the memory alert path.
1) 用 iftop 或 nethogs 定位占用带宽最高的进程/连接；2) K: 1) Use iftop or nethogs to find the processes/connections consuming the most bandwidth; 2) On Kubernetes nodes, check whether a Pod is doing bulk data transfer (backup, data sync, image pull); 3) Confirm whether the NIC is saturated and throttle or reschedule if so; 4) For abnormal traffic, check for a misconfiguration causing a traffic loop.
1) 用 iftop/nethogs 定位占用带宽最高的连接；2) K8s 节点: 1) Use iftop/nethogs to find the connections consuming the most bandwidth; 2) On Kubernetes nodes, check for high-traffic Pods or large image pulls; 3) Move deferrable jobs off peak; 4) If more bandwidth is genuinely needed, upgrade the NIC or move some workloads.
1) 用 iostat -x 1 看 r_await/w_await 与队列深度: 1) Run iostat -x 1 and look at r_await/w_await and queue depth; 2) High latency with low IOPS suggests a disk hardware problem — check with smartctl -a; 3) If IOPS is also high, treat it as disk saturation and find the heavy IO process; 4) For cloud disks, check whether the specification's IOPS/throughput ceiling triggered throttling.
1) 用 iostat -x 1 确认是哪块盘、await 与 %util；2): 1) Run iostat -x 1 to see which disk it is and the actual await and %util; 2) Run iotop -oP to find the process doing the most IO; 3) On Kubernetes nodes it is usually container log writes, image pull/unpack, or one Pod's data writes; 4) Move deferrable work off peak; for sustained load, consider SSDs or spreading the data.
1) 用 ip -s link show \u003c网卡\u003e 与 et: 1) Run ip -s link show <nic> and ethtool -S <nic> for the error counters and types; 2) Confirm the negotiated speed and duplex match the peer; 3) Check the cable/optical module, or open a cloud provider ticket; 4) If redundancy exists, move traffic away first.
1) 用 kubeadm certs check-expiration（kube: 1) Run kubeadm certs check-expiration (kubeadm clusters) or openssl x509 -noout -dates to confirm the expiry; 2) On kubeadm clusters run kubeadm certs renew all and restart the control plane components; 3) kubelet client certificates usually rotate automatically — if not, check the rotateCertificates setting and CSR approval; 4) After renewal, verify the components loaded the new certificate (restart them) and re-check every node.
1) 用 kubectl get node -o wide 对比各节点内核版本；: 1) Run kubectl get node -o wide to compare kernel versions; 2) Determine whether the difference is temporary (mid-upgrade) or long standing; 3) Bring the lagging nodes' kernels in line step by step; 4) Before upgrading, confirm the container runtime and CNI plugin support the target kernel.
1) 用 sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_c: 1) Run sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_count and nf_conntrack_max to check the level; 2) On Kubernetes nodes, kube-proxy in iptables mode creates many conntrack entries, especially at high Pod density; 3) Raise nf_conntrack_max and the bucket count together; 4) Longer term, consider switching to IPVS mode to reduce conntrack pressure.
1) 用 top 或 vmstat 确认 st 列的持续水位；2) 这是宿主机层: 1) Use top or vmstat to confirm the sustained level of the st column; 2) This is contention at the hypervisor level and cannot be fixed from inside the VM; 3) In the cloud, contact the provider or move to a dedicated instance type (no steal); 4) On self-hosted virtualization, check the host's overcommit ratio and migrate VMs.
1) 用 uptime 看 1/5/15 分钟趋势判断是突发还是持续；2) to: 1) Run uptime to see the 1/5/15 minute trend and judge spike versus sustained; 2) Check %wa in top — high means the bottleneck is disk rather than CPU; 3) Use the r/b columns in vmstat 1 to separate CPU-bound from IO-blocked; 4) On Kubernetes nodes use kubectl top pod to find the heavy Pods and consider moving them.
1) 用 vmstat 1 看 si/so 列确认是否已在 swap；2) 用: 1) Run vmstat 1 and check the si/so columns for swapping; 2) Use sar -B or /proc/vmstat to watch pgmajfault growth; 3) Find the heaviest process or Pod and assess whether it can be moved; 4) Review the swap setting — Kubernetes nodes normally have swap disabled, since enabling it masks memory problems.
1) 用 vmstat 1 确认 cs 列的水位；2) 用 pidstat -w: 1) Run vmstat 1 and check the cs column; 2) Run pidstat -w 1 to find the processes switching most; 3) Common root causes are too many threads, heavy lock contention, or many short-lived processes; 4) Reducing thread pool sizes and lock granularity in the application is the real fix.
1) 登录节点执行 systemctl status kubelet 确认进程状: 1) On the node run systemctl status kubelet to check the process; 2) Use journalctl -u kubelet -n 200 --no-pager to find the exit or error reason; 3) Common causes are expired certificates, config errors and an unavailable container runtime; 4) After recovery, confirm the node is Ready again and check whether Pods were wrongly evicted meanwhile.
1) 登录节点用 crictl ps 与 crictl info 确认容器运行时: 1) On the node run crictl ps and crictl info to gauge container runtime responsiveness; 2) Check whether the node has too many containers and whether disk IO is saturated — these are the main causes of slow PLEG; 3) For a stalled runtime, consider restarting containerd (briefly affects that node); 4) If it persists, reduce the Pod density on that node.
1) 登录节点用 df -h 定位挂载点，通常是 /var/lib/docker: 1) On the node run df -h to find the mount point, usually /var/lib/docker or /var/lib/containerd; 2) Run crictl rmi --prune or docker system prune to clean unused image layers — the fastest win; 3) Check whether a Pod is writing large amounts of data to an emptyDir or hostPath; 4) After cleaning, confirm the kubelet DiskPressure taint was removed automatically.
1) 登录节点用 free -h 确认 available 与 swap；2): 1) On the node run free -h to check available memory and swap; 2) Run ps aux --sort=-%mem | head for the biggest consumers; 3) On Kubernetes nodes, prefer kubectl top pod -A --sort-by=memory to find the Pod; 4) For a leak, fix it in the application; for capacity, move Pods off or add nodes.
1) 看 Prometheus 日志中 remote_write 或 tsdb: 1) Check the Prometheus log for remote_write or tsdb errors; 2) For remote write failures, confirm remote storage availability and credentials, and check for throttling; 3) For local storage failures, check disk space and permissions — a corrupted TSDB may require clearing the WAL; 4) Confirm the queue backlog is draining; if not, raise queue_config or reduce the write volume.
1) 看 apiserver 的错误码与延迟分布，确认是读还是写请求在劣化；2): 1) Look at the apiserver error code and latency distribution to tell read from write degradation; 2) For write degradation, check etcd disk latency first — that is the most common root cause; 3) For read degradation, look for clients doing wide LIST calls (full enumeration without a resourceVersion); 4) Rate limit the offending client and consider enabling APF (API Priority and Fairness).
1) 看 kubelet 日志中 certificate rotation 相关: 1) Check the kubelet log for certificate rotation errors; 2) Check whether CSRs are stuck Pending: kubectl get csr, and approve manually with kubectl certificate approve if needed; 3) Confirm the cluster has a CSR auto-approval controller (kube-controller-manager's --cluster-signing-cert-file setting); 4) After fixing, confirm new CSRs are auto-approved and signed.
1) 看日志中 compaction 相关报错；2) 最常见是磁盘空间不足——先: 1) Check the log for compaction errors; 2) The most common cause is insufficient disk space — confirm the free space first; 3) A corrupted block may need its directory deleted (losing that time range); 4) After fixing, confirm subsequent compactions complete successfully.
1) 看日志中 reload 相关报错与涉及的 block；2) 常见为数据块损: 1) Check the log for reload errors and which block is involved; 2) It is usually a corrupted block or a permissions problem; 3) For permissions, fix the data directory owner; a corrupted block can only be deleted (losing that time range); 4) After fixing, restart Prometheus and confirm the data is queryable.
1) 看日志中 rule evaluation 相关的超时报错；2) 找出评估耗: 1) Check the log for rule evaluation timeout errors; 2) Find the rule group with the longest evaluation time, usually recording rules with heavy queries; 3) Split the rule group, lengthen evaluation_interval, or optimise the queries in the rules; 4) If resources are short, scale Prometheus.
1) 看日志中 target sync 的具体报错；2) 常见为 relabel: 1) Check the log for the specific target sync error; 2) It is usually a relabel misconfiguration producing an invalid target address; 3) Review recently changed ServiceMonitor/PodMonitor configurations; 4) After fixing, confirm the targets are healthy again on the /targets page.
1) 看日志中失败规则的名称与错误；2) 常见为规则里的查询语法错误、引用了不存: 1) Check the log for the failing rule name and error; 2) Common causes are a query syntax error in the rule, a reference to a non-existent metric, or an oversized result; 3) Validate the rule files with promtool check rules; 4) After fixing, confirm the rule shows ok on the /rules page.
1) 看日志中服务发现相关的报错；2) K8s SD 的检查 Prometheu: 1) Check the log for service discovery errors; 2) For Kubernetes SD, check that Prometheus's RBAC covers the required resources; 3) For other SD types (Consul, file, …), check backend reachability and credentials; 4) After fixing, confirm the target list is updated on the /service-discovery page.
1) 确认是哪个目标在上报乱序数据；2) 常见根因是目标机器时钟不同步，或指标由: 1) Identify which target is reporting out-of-order data; 2) The usual root causes are an unsynchronised clock on the target, or metrics aggregated from multiple sources with mixed timestamps; 3) Correct the target machine's clock first (chronyc); 4) For Pushgateway-style setups, review how the pusher handles timestamps.
5分钟内apiserver的请求数统计: Apiserver request count in the last 5 minutes
CPU steal time 偏高，说明宿主机上有其他虚拟机在抢占 CPU，本机: CPU steal time is high, which means other virtual machines on the hypervisor are competing for CPU and this machine gets less compute than expected.
CPU 使用量除以 CPU 请求量。若没有数据需要检查相应容器是否进行了 CPU: CPU usage divided by CPU request. If there is no data, check whether the container has a CPU Request configured.
CPU 使用量除以 CPU 限制量。若没有数据需要检查相应容器是否进行了 CPU: CPU usage divided by CPU limit. If there is no data, check whether the container has a CPU Limit configured.
DaemonSet 没有在应有的节点上调度，那些节点缺少该 DaemonSet: The DaemonSet is not scheduled on nodes where it should run; those nodes lack the capability it provides (log collection, networking, monitoring, …).
DaemonSet 的滚动更新卡住，部分节点仍在跑旧版本，节点间行为不一致。: The DaemonSet rollout is stuck: some nodes still run the old version and behaviour differs across nodes.
DaemonSet 被调度到了不该运行的节点上，会浪费资源，也可能在不兼容的节点: The DaemonSet was scheduled onto nodes where it should not run, wasting resources and possibly erroring on incompatible nodes.
Deployment Pod 可用性不足70%（replica超过9个pod）: Deployment Pod availability below 70% (replicas above 9 pods)
Deployment 历史更新保留版本的数量: Number of revision history versions retained by the Deployment
Deployment 的实际副本数与期望不符，服务容量低于预期，滚动发布可能卡住: The Deployment's actual replica count does not match the desired count: service capacity is below expectations and the rollout may be stuck.
Deployment 的滚动发布卡住，新版本没有推进完成，集群里同时存在新旧两个: The Deployment rollout is stuck: the new version has not finished rolling out and both old and new versions are running in the cluster.
HPA 已经扩到最大副本数，说明当前配置的上限已经无法承载流量，再有增长只能靠降: The HPA has scaled to its maximum replica count, which means the configured ceiling can no longer carry the traffic — further growth needs degradation or rate limiting.
HPA 的实际副本数与它计算出的期望副本数不符，说明扩缩容没能执行，容量调整失效: The HPA's actual replica count does not match the count it computed, which means scaling did not execute and capacity adjustment is not working.
Job 执行失败，它负责的任务（数据处理、定时清理、迁移等）没有完成。: The Job failed: the task it owns (data processing, scheduled cleanup, migration, …) did not complete.
Job 长时间未完成，它负责的任务迟迟没有结束，下游依赖会一直等待。: The Job has not completed for a long time: the task it owns is dragging on and downstream dependencies keep waiting.
Kubernetes 客户端请求错误率偏高，说明某个组件在频繁调用 apiser: The Kubernetes client error rate is elevated, which means a component's calls to apiserver keep failing and its functionality may already be broken.
PersistentVolume 处于 Failed 或 Pending 异常状: The PersistentVolume is in a Failed or Pending state and Pods depending on it cannot start or cannot read/write data.
PersistentVolume 的 inode 即将耗尽，耗尽后即使有剩余空间: PersistentVolume inodes are close to exhaustion; once exhausted, no new file can be created even with free space.
PersistentVolume 空间即将耗尽。PV 写满后应用写入直接失败，且: PersistentVolume space is close to exhaustion. Once a PV is full, application writes fail outright, and many storage types cannot be expanded online, making recovery expensive.
Pod 启动耗时过长，滚动发布与扩容都会被拖慢，故障恢复时间也会拉长。: Pod startup is taking too long, which slows down rolling releases and scaling and lengthens recovery time.
Pod 在反复重启（CrashLoopBackOff），服务实际不可用，且会持续: The Pod is restarting repeatedly (CrashLoopBackOff): the service is effectively unavailable and it keeps consuming node resources and image pull bandwidth.
Pod 长时间不处于 Ready 状态，它承载的流量无法被 Service 转发: The Pod has been not Ready for a long time: its traffic cannot be routed by the Service, and a shortfall in replicas directly reduces service capacity.
Prometheus Operator 出现异常，它管理的 Prometheus: Prometheus Operator is failing: the Prometheus/Alertmanager configuration it manages may not sync correctly, so monitoring configuration changes will not take effect.
Prometheus 到 Alertmanager 的告警投递出现问题。这意味着: Alert delivery from Prometheus to Alertmanager is failing. This means rules may be firing while the alerts never get out — a blind spot in the monitoring system itself.
Prometheus 收到乱序时间戳的样本并丢弃，部分数据正在丢失。: Prometheus is receiving and discarding out-of-order timestamped samples; some data is being lost.
Prometheus 收到重复时间戳的样本并丢弃，说明有目标被重复抓取，部分数据: Prometheus is receiving and discarding duplicate timestamped samples, which means a target is being scraped twice and some data is being lost.
Prometheus 查询负载过高，查询队列接近饱和，仪表盘会变慢，告警规则评估: Prometheus query load is too high and the query queue is near saturation: dashboards will slow down and rule evaluations may time out and be skipped.
Prometheus 没有在写入任何样本，监控数据完全中断——所有基于它的告警都: Prometheus is not ingesting any samples: monitoring data is completely interrupted and every alert based on it has stopped working.
Prometheus 的远程写入或本地存储出现失败，监控数据正在丢失。: Prometheus remote write or local storage is failing and monitoring data is being lost.
Prometheus 跳过了规则评估，意味着这段时间的告警规则没有被计算——期间: Prometheus skipped rule evaluations, which means alert rules were not computed for that period — failures during it produced no alerts.
Prometheus 配置加载失败，最近一次配置变更没有生效，抓取目标与告警规则: Prometheus failed to load its configuration: the most recent change did not take effect and the scrape targets and alert rules are still the old ones.
RSS + 部分活跃的 page cache（不能立即回收）， 更应该关注此指标: RSS + part of the active page cache (cannot be reclaimed immediately); this is the metric to focus on
StatefulSet 的实际副本数与期望不符。有状态服务的副本是按序启动的，一: The StatefulSet's actual replica count does not match the desired count. Stateful replicas start in order, so one stuck replica blocks all the rest.
StatefulSet 的更新没有推进完成，部分副本仍在跑旧版本。: The StatefulSet update has not finished rolling out and some replicas still run the old version.
TSDB 压缩失败，磁盘占用会持续增长且查询性能会下降，长期可能导致 Prome: TSDB compaction is failing: disk usage will keep growing and query performance will degrade, eventually making Prometheus unusable.
TSDB 数据块重载失败，部分历史数据可能无法查询。: TSDB block reload is failing and some historical data may be unqueryable.
apiserver 主动终止了部分请求，说明已触发 APF（优先级与公平性）限流: The apiserver is terminating requests, which means APF (Priority and Fairness) throttling or timeout protection has kicked in and some client requests are failing.
apiserver 的错误预算消耗速率过快，说明请求错误率或延迟已明显偏离 SL: The apiserver is burning its error budget too fast, which means the request error rate or latency has clearly deviated from the SLO and the control plane is degrading.
apiserver工作队列深度，越接近0越好: Apiserver work queue depth; the closer to 0 the better
apiserver的5xx 错误率(5xx请求数/总请求数): Apiserver 5xx error rate (5xx requests / total requests)
apiserver的5xx错误率，按请求动作分类统计: Apiserver 5xx error rate by request verb
apiserver的响应延迟，按请求动作分类统计: Apiserver response latency by request verb
apiserver的实例健康状态，0表示down，1表示up: Apiserver instance health status; 0 means down, 1 means up

controller manager zone中的node数据: Controller manager Node count per zone

coredns 请求量，按请求类型统计: CoreDNS request count by request type
etcd 处理的请求数，按响应码统计: etcd handled request count by response code
etcd处理的请求数， 按实例统计: etcd handled request count by instance
etcd处理的请求数，按请求类型统计: etcd handled request count by request type
etcd读取索引失败 读取索引慢（过期索引或者超时）次数: etcd read index failure and slow read index count (stale index or timeout)
kube-apiserver 不可达。apiserver 是集群唯一的入口，不可: kube-apiserver is unreachable. It is the cluster's only entry point, so every control plane operation (deploy, scale, schedule) is stalled.
kube-controller-manager 不可达。各类控制器停摆意味着副本: kube-controller-manager is unreachable. With the controllers stalled, replica maintenance, node lifecycle and endpoint updates all stop working.
kube-scheduler 不可达。调度器停摆意味着新 Pod 无法被分配到节: kube-scheduler is unreachable. With the scheduler stalled, new Pods cannot be assigned to nodes and both scaling and self-healing stop working (running Pods are unaffected).
kubelet 不可达，该节点已脱离控制面管理，无法创建、更新或删除 Pod。: kubelet is unreachable: the node has left control plane management and Pods cannot be created, updated or deleted on it.
kubelet 的 PLEG（Pod 生命周期事件生成器）耗时过高，说明容器运行: kubelet PLEG (Pod Lifecycle Event Generator) duration is too high, which means the container runtime is responding slowly and kubelet may soon mark the node NotReady.
node_exporter 的 textfile collector 抓取出错，: The node_exporter textfile collector is erroring: custom metrics cannot be reported and alerts based on them stop working.
pod进入调度队列的平均速率: Average rate of Pods entering the scheduling queue
scheduler 90分位请求延迟，按实例统计: Scheduler P90 request latency by instance
scheduler 90分位请求延迟，按请求类型统计: Scheduler P90 request latency by request type
scheduler 请求量 按返回码统计: Scheduler request count by response code
scheduler请求量，按请求类型统计: Scheduler request count by request type
上下文切换次数异常偏高，CPU 大量时间花在调度而非实际计算上，有效算力下降。: Context switches are abnormally high: the CPU spends a large share of its time scheduling rather than computing, reducing effective capacity.
主机 inode 将在 24 小时内填满 (instance {{ $label: Host inodes will fill up within 24 hours (instance {{ $labels.instance }})
主机上发生了 OOM Kill，有进程被内核强制杀死。K8s 节点上这通常意味着: An OOM kill occurred on the host and a process was killed by the kernel. On a Kubernetes node this usually means a container exceeded its memory limit or the node is short on memory overall.
主机上有 systemd 服务处于失败状态，该服务提供的功能已经中断。: A systemd service on the host has failed and the functionality it provides is down.
主机内存压力大，内核正在频繁回收页面（major page fault 上升），: The host is under memory pressure: the kernel is reclaiming pages frequently (rising major page faults) and overall responsiveness will degrade.
主机可用内存不足，继续下降会触发 swap 抖动甚至 OOM Killer 杀进: Host available memory is insufficient; further decline will cause swap thrashing or get processes killed by the OOM killer.
主机时钟偏差或未同步。K8s 对时钟一致性要求很高，偏差会导致证书校验失败、事件: The host clock is skewed or unsynchronised. Kubernetes is very sensitive to clock agreement — skew breaks certificate validation, scrambles event ordering and disrupts leases.
主机磁盘将在 24 小时内填满: Host disk will fill up within 24 hours
主机磁盘将在 24 小时内填满 (instance {{ $labels.ins: Host disk will fill up within 24 hours (instance {{ $labels.instance }})
主机磁盘空间不足。K8s 节点磁盘写满会触发 kubelet 驱逐 Pod 并停: Host disk space is insufficient. A full Kubernetes node disk makes kubelet evict Pods and stop pulling images, and the node quickly becomes unusable.
主机磁盘读写延迟异常，IO 请求排队严重，上层应用会出现明显卡顿。: Host disk read/write latency is abnormal: IO requests are queueing badly and upper-layer applications will stall noticeably.
主机磁盘读写速率异常偏高，磁盘可能已成为瓶颈，所有依赖它的操作都会变慢。: Host disk read/write rate is abnormally high: the disk may already be the bottleneck and everything depending on it will slow down.
主机网卡出现错包，通常是物理链路问题，会导致重传与延迟抖动。: The host NIC is seeing error packets, usually a physical link problem causing retransmits and latency jitter.
主机网络吞吐量异常，接近网卡能力上限时会出现丢包与延迟抖动。: Host network throughput is abnormal; approaching the NIC's capacity brings packet loss and latency jitter.
交换分区即将用满。swap 用满后内核只能靠 OOM Killer 释放内存，会: Swap is close to full. Once swap is exhausted the kernel can only free memory through the OOM killer, and processes will be forcibly killed.
任务在队列中的90分位等待耗时: P90 time work items spend waiting in the queue
兼容阿里ACK和categraf采集的指标: Compatible with metrics collected by Alibaba ACK and Categraf
内存使用量除以内存请求量。若没有数据需要检查相应容器是否进行了 Memory R: Memory usage divided by memory request. If there is no data, check whether the container has a Memory Request configured.
内存使用量除以内存限制量。若没有数据需要检查相应容器是否进行了 Memory L: Memory usage divided by memory limit. If there is no data, check whether the container has a Memory Limit configured.
内核连接跟踪表接近上限，表满后新连接会被直接丢弃，表现为大面积连接超时。: The kernel connection tracking table is close to its limit; once full, new connections are dropped outright and you see widespread connection timeouts.
告警规则评估失败，这些规则对应的告警不会触发——相关故障将无人知晓。: Alert rule evaluation is failing: the alerts for those rules will not fire, so the corresponding failures will go unnoticed.
命名空间的资源配额接近或已经用满，新 Pod 将无法创建，扩容与发布都会失败。: The namespace resource quota is close to or already full: new Pods cannot be created and both scaling and releases will fail.
实际“工作集内存”，即真正被频繁访问、内核不愿回收的内存，OOM 风险监控: The actual working set memory, i.e. memory that is frequently accessed and that the kernel is reluctant to reclaim; used to monitor OOM risk
容器 CPU 使用率超过 limit 的 80%，接近配额上限后会被 CFS 限: Container CPU usage is above 80% of its limit; near the quota it will be CFS-throttled and application response times will lengthen noticeably.
容器 CPU 使用量相对于限制量/请求量的比例。若没有数据需要检查相应容器是否进: Container CPU usage as a ratio of its limit/request. If there is no data, check whether the container has a CPU Limit/Request configured.
容器 CPU 被大量限流（CFS throttling），说明 CPU limi: The container is being heavily CFS-throttled, which means the CPU limit is insufficient and application response times will lengthen and become jittery.
容器 WorkingSet 内存使用量相对于限制量/请求量的比例。若没有数据需要: Container WorkingSet memory usage as a ratio of its limit/request. If there is no data, check whether the container has a Memory Limit/Request configured.

容器长时间处于 Waiting 状态，Pod 起不来，服务容量不足。: The container has been Waiting for a long time: the Pod cannot start and service capacity is short.

服务发现刷新失败，目标列表可能已经过时——新上线的实例不会被采集，已下线的还在被: Service discovery refresh is failing: the target list may be stale — newly launched instances will not be scraped and decommissioned ones are still being scraped.

目标同步失败，部分目标的抓取配置没能生效，这些目标的数据可能缺失。: Target sync failed: the scrape configuration for some targets did not take effect and their data may be missing.
网络接口接近饱和，链路带宽已经不够用，会出现丢包、排队与延迟抖动。: The network interface is close to saturation: link bandwidth is no longer sufficient and you will see packet loss, queueing and latency jitter.
网络接口状态抖动，链路反复 up/down。每次抖动都会中断该链路上的连接并触发: The network interface is flapping up and down. Each flap interrupts connections on that link and triggers route reconvergence.
聚合 API（APIService）不可用，依赖它的功能完全失效——例如 met: The aggregated API (APIService) is unavailable and everything depending on it stops working — for example, a failed metrics-server breaks both kubectl top and HPA.
聚合 API（APIService）调用出现错误，依赖该扩展 API 的功能会异: Aggregated API (APIService) calls are erroring and functionality depending on that extension API will misbehave.
聚合 API（APIService）调用出现错误，依赖该扩展 API 的功能（如: Aggregated API (APIService) calls are erroring and functionality depending on that extension API (metrics-server, custom metrics, …) will misbehave.
节点 CPU 使用率超过 90%，其上所有 Pod 都会争抢 CPU，请求排队、: Node CPU utilization is above 90%: every Pod on it competes for CPU, so requests queue and latency rises.
节点上的 Pod 数量接近 kubelet 的上限，触顶后新 Pod 无法调度到: The Pod count on the node is close to the kubelet limit; once it tops out no new Pod can be scheduled there and node management overhead rises significantly.
节点不可达，控制面已经联系不上它。其上 Pod 的真实状态未知，会在容忍期后被标: The node is unreachable and the control plane can no longer contact it. The true state of its Pods is unknown and they will be marked for eviction after the toleration period.
节点内存使用率超过 90%，继续增长会触发 kubelet 驱逐 Pod，甚至系: Node memory utilization is above 90%; further growth triggers kubelet Pod eviction and possibly a system-level OOM.
节点在 Ready 与 NotReady 之间反复抖动。每次抖动都会触发 Pod: The node is flapping between Ready and NotReady. Each flap triggers Pod eviction and rescheduling, which is more destructive than a sustained outage.
节点处于 NotReady 状态，其上的 Pod 会在容忍期后被驱逐重建，服务容: The node is NotReady: its Pods will be evicted and recreated after the toleration period and service capacity drops.
节点磁盘使用率超过 90%，kubelet 会开始驱逐 Pod 并停止拉取新镜像: Node disk utilization is above 90%: kubelet will start evicting Pods and stop pulling images, and the node will soon become unusable.

证书即将过期。Kubernetes 组件间全部依赖 mTLS，证书过期会导致对应: A certificate is about to expire. Kubernetes components all rely on mTLS, so an expired certificate takes the corresponding component offline — a completely avoidable self-inflicted outage.
证书自动续签失败。续签一直失败意味着证书最终会过期，届时该组件会直接失联。: Automatic certificate renewal is failing. Continued failure means the certificate will eventually expire and that component will go offline.
该值大于0，说明CPU在运行期间发生throttle情况，即容器设置的CPU规格: A value greater than 0 means CPU throttling occurred at runtime, i.e. the CPU spec configured for the container does not meet its actual CPU demand. In this case you usually need to raise the container CPU spec, or optimize the program to reduce CPU cost.

队列中最耗时任务的处理时间（500ms采样周期，未完成的任务-任务开始处理即出队: Processing time of the longest-running work item in the queue (500ms sampling period, unfinished items, timed from the moment the item is dequeued and starts processing)
集群内组件版本不一致。版本偏差过大会引发 API 兼容性问题与难以排查的异常行为: Component versions in the cluster are inconsistent. A large version skew causes API compatibility problems and hard-to-diagnose behaviour.
集群内节点的内核版本不一致。内核差异会导致同一份工作负载在不同节点上表现不同，是: Kernel versions differ across cluster nodes. Kernel differences make the same workload behave differently on different nodes and are a hard-to-diagnose source of problems.
集群资源已超卖：所有 Pod 的 requests 之和超过了集群可分配容量。此: Cluster resources are overcommitted: the sum of all Pod requests exceeds allocatable capacity. If a node fails now, the evicted Pods will have nowhere to be scheduled.
